hook.en: A deposit of ₹1,000 growing at 10% a year becomes 1000, 1100, 1210 and so on. Each year it is multiplied by the same 1.1. That is a *geometric progression*.
hook.kn: ವರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ 10% ಬೆಳೆಯುವ ₹1,000 ಠೇವಣಿ 1000, 1100, 1210 ಹೀಗೆ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಷವೂ ಅದೇ 1.1 ರಿಂದ ಗುಣಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದೇ ಗುಣೋತ್ತರ ಶ್ರೇಢಿ.

title.en: Recognise a G.P. and its common ratio
Use aₙ = arⁿ⁻¹ and b² = ac

say.en: A deposit of 1,000 rupees growing at 10 percent a year becomes 1000, 1100, 1210 and so on. Each year it is multiplied by the same 1.1. That is a geometric progression. In this lesson: Recognise a G.P. and its common ratio.
Use a n equals ar to the power n to the power minus 1 and b squared equals ac.

body.en: A sequence of non-zero terms is a G.P. if the ratio of every term to the one before it is a constant $r$, the common ratio. With first term $a$ the G.P. is $a, ar, ar^2, \dots$ and the $n$th term is $a_n = ar^{n-1}$. The $n$th term from the end of a finite G.P. with last term $l$ is $l / r^{n-1}$.
body.kn: ಯಾವುದೇ ಪದವನ್ನು ಹಿಂದಿನ ಪದದಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಿದಾಗ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಅನುಪಾತ r ಸಿಗುವ ಅನುಕ್ರಮವೇ ಗುಣೋತ್ತರ ಶ್ರೇಢಿ. ಮೊದಲ ಪದ a ಆಗಿದ್ದರೆ n ನೇ ಪದ a rⁿ⁻¹.

narration.en: In a G.P. each term is the previous term multiplied by the same number r. The nth term is a times r to the power n minus one.

body.en: Three non-zero *numbers* $a, b, c$ are in G.P. exactly when $b^2 = ac$. When three unknown terms in G.P. are needed, take them as $\frac{a}{r}, a, ar$: their product is simply $a^3$.

problem.en: Find the 10th term and the nth term of the G.P. 5, 25, 125, …

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the 10th term and the nth term of the G.P. 5, 25, 125, …

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the 10th term and the nth term of the G.P. 5, 25, 125,...
a equals 5 and r equals 25 over 5 equals 5.
a n equals 5 times 5 to the power n to the power minus 1 equals 5 to the power n.
a 10 equals 5 to the power 10 equals 9765625.
So the answer is a 10 equals 5 to the power 10 equals 9765625; a n equals 5 to the power n.

problem.en: Which term of the G.P. 2, 2√2, 4, … is 128?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Which term of the G.P. 2, 2√2, 4, … is 128?

say.en: Let us solve this together. Which term of the G.P. 2, 2 the square root of 2, 4,... is 128?
a equals 2, r equals the square root of 2.
2the square root of 2 to the power n to the power minus 1 equals 128 gives the square root of 2 to the power n to the power minus 1 equals 64 equals the square root of 2 to the power 12.
So n minus 1 equals 12 and n equals 13.
So the answer is The 13th term.

say.en: Divide two terms to find r. If the mth and nth terms are given, divide them: a m over a n equals r to the power m to the power -n. The first term cancels. For example a 6 over a 3 equals r cubed.
